source_refs.note: Topic 16.2.2 with Figure 16.2 (printed at the top of the page), printed page 338.

blocks.alt: Nine red-bordered diamond pictograms, five in the top row and four below, each named underneath: Explosive (a bursting bomb), Flammable (a flame over a line), Oxidizing (a flame over a circle), Compressed Gas (a gas cylinder), Corrosive (liquid dripping from two tubes onto a surface and a hand); Toxic (a skull and crossbones), Irritant (an exclamation mark), Environmentally Damaging (a dead tree and a dead fish) and Health hazard (a person with a star on the chest).
blocks.caption: Figure 16.2: Pictogram of chemical hazards (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 16.2).

blocks.text: A laboratory worker must use the chemicals according to the standard procedures keeping in view the particular hazards and precautions required for the safe use.
